body.statement: For every invertible diagonal \(D_n\) and every \(m_n\in\mathbb R^{2r}\), the interval \([\sigma^2Z_{p,n}^{\top}D_nZ_{q,n}-\sigma^2W_n,\sigma^2Z_{p,n}^{\top}D_nZ_{q,n}+\sigma^2W_n]\) covers \(\sigma^2m_{p,n}^{\top}D_nm_{q,n}\) with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), has expected length at most \(K_\alpha\sigma^2(s(m_n)+\|D_n\|_{\mathrm{op}})\), and its length divided by \(2\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\sigma^2s(m_n)\) converges to one along every sequence with \(s(m_n)/\|D_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to\infty\).
body.justification: A single analytic formula replaces nonlinear endpoint optimization while preserving exact finite-dimensional coverage and the regular Gaussian constant.
body.gap: Bei--Navjeevan establish general minimum-distance validity, but not this explicit outer formula or its every-diverging-sequence length limit.
body.consumer: Applied panel routines can evaluate the interval using one SVD and scalar special functions.
